source_text: Arjuna saw standing there fathers and grandfathers, teachers,uncles, brothers, sons and grandsons, and also companions;And fathers-in-law and friends in both the armies. Seeing all these thus arrayed, Arjuna,Filled with the utmost compassion, sorrowfully spoke: Seeing my own kinsmen, O Krsna a, arrayed and wishing to fight,My limbs collapse, my mouth dries up, there is trembling in my body and my hair stands on end; The bow Gandiva slips from my hand and my skin also is burning; I am not able to stand still, my mind is whirling.And I see evil portents, O Krsna, and I foresee no good in slaying my own kinsmen in the fight.I do not desire victory, O Krsna, nor kingdom, nor pleasure. Of what use is kingdom to us, O Krsna, of what use pleasure or life? Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, pleasures and happiness, they are arrayed here in battle, having renounced their lives and riches. Teachers, fathers, sons, and also grandfathers; uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and other kinsmen; These I do not wish to kill, though they kill me, O Krsna; even forthe kingdom of the three worlds; how much less then for the sake ofthe earth!
source_summary: Arjuna becomes overwhelmed with sorrow, fear and confusion when he sees his relatives, teachers and friends on the opposing side of the battlefield. He questions the value of victory and worldly pleasures when achieving them would mean fighting his loved ones.
english_explanation: Arjuna becomes emotionally overwhelmed when he sees his relatives, teachers and friends standing against him in battle. He experiences fear, sorrow, confusion and physical discomfort, and begins questioning the purpose of fighting when it means harming the people he loves. This passage illustrates how difficult situations and conflicts between personal relationships and responsibilities can disturb a person's mind and decision-making.
hindi_explanation: जब अर्जुन युद्धभूमि में अपने रिश्तेदारों, गुरुओं और मित्रों को अपने सामने देखता है, तो वह भावनात्मक रूप से विचलित हो जाता है। उसके मन में भय, दुख और भ्रम उत्पन्न होता है। वह सोचने लगता है कि जिन लोगों से वह प्रेम करता है, उनके विरुद्ध युद्ध करने का क्या अर्थ है। यह प्रसंग दिखाता है कि कठिन परिस्थितियों और व्यक्तिगत संबंधों तथा जिम्मेदारियों के बीच संघर्ष होने पर व्यक्ति का मन किस प्रकार अशांत हो सकता है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Emotional distress and moral conflict can cloud judgment; pause and examine the situation before deciding how to act.

source_text: The Blessed Lord said: Thou grievest for those thou shouldst not grieve for, and yet thou speakest words that sound like wisdom. Wise men do not mourn for the dead or for the living.Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor thou, nor these rulers of men; nor will there ever be a time hereafter when we shall all cease to be.As the soul in the body passes through childhood, youth and old age, so (after departure from this body) it passes on to another body.The sage is not bewildered by this.Contacts with the objects of the senses, O Arjuna, give rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go, they are impermanent; endure them, O Arjuna.The man who is not troubled by these contacts, O Arjuna, who treats alike pleasure and pain, who is wise; he is fit for immortality.Of non-being there is no coming to be; of being there is no ceasing to be. The truth about both is seen by the seers of truth.Know that by which all this is pervaded is indestructible, and that no one can cause the destruction of this immutable being.It is said that (only) these bodies of the eternal embodied soul,which is indestructible and incomprehensible, are perishable.Therefore fight, O Arjuna! He who thinks that this soul is a slayer, and he who thinks that this soul is slain; both of them are ignorant. This soul neither slays nor is slain.It is never born, nor does it die, nor having once been, will it againcease to be. It is unborn, eternal, and everlasting. This primeval one is not slain when the body is slain.He who knows that it is indestructible and eternal, unborn and unchanging, how can that man slay, O Arjuna, or cause another to slay? Just as a man casts off worn-out clothes and takes on others that are new, so the embodied soul casts off worn-out bodies and takes on others that are new.Weapons do not cut it, nor does fire burn it; waters do not make it wet, nor does wind make it dry.It is uncleavable; it cannot be burnt, it can neither be wetted nor dried. It is eternal, omnipresent, unchanging and immovable. It is everlasting.It is called unmanifest, unthinkable and immutable; therefore,knowing it as such, thou shouldst not grieve.
source_summary: Krishna explains that the Self is eternal, unborn and indestructible, while the physical body is subject to change. He teaches Arjuna not to identify the eternal Self with the temporary body.
english_explanation: Krishna explains that the Self is not limited to the present body or a particular moment in time. The passage introduces the distinction between the enduring Self and the changing physical body.
hindi_explanation: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि आत्मा का अस्तित्व केवल वर्तमान शरीर या समय तक सीमित नहीं है। यह प्रसंग शाश्वत आत्मा और बदलते हुए शरीर के बीच अंतर को समझाता है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: The Self is eternal and distinct from the changing physical body; understanding this distinction can change how we relate to grief and change.

source_text: As much use as there is for a pond when there is everywhere a flood, so much is there in all the Vedas for a brahmin who understands.In action only hast thou a right and never in its fruits. Let not thy motive be the fruits of action; nor let thy attachment be to inaction.Fixed in yoga, O Arjuna, perform actions, abandoning attachment and remaining even-minded in success and failure; for serenity of mind is called yoga.Mere action is far inferior to the discipline of intelligence, O Arjuna. Seek refuge in intelligence; pitiful are those whose motive is the fruit of action.One who has disciplined his intelligence leaves behind in this world both good and evil deeds. Therefore strive for yoga, for yoga is skill in action.Having disciplined their intelligence and having abandoned the fruit born of their action, the wise are freed from the bondage of birth and attain the state that is free from sorrow.When thy intelligence shall cross the tangle of delusion, then thou shalt become indifferent to what shall be heard and to what has been heard (in the Veda).When thy intelligence, which is now perplexed by the Vedic texts,shall stand immovable and be fixed in concentration, then shalt thou attain yoga.
source_summary: Krishna teaches Arjuna to focus on performing his actions rather than becoming attached to their results. This can be applied to work, studies and personal goals by giving sincere effort without allowing the outcome to control one's peace of mind.
english_explanation: Krishna teaches Arjuna to focus on performing his actions rather than becoming attached to their results. This can be applied to work, studies and personal goals by giving sincere effort without allowing the outcome to control one's peace of mind.
hindi_explanation: कृष्ण अर्जुन को सिखाते हैं कि व्यक्ति का अधिकार अपने कर्म पर है, उसके फल पर नहीं। इसे काम, पढ़ाई और व्यक्तिगत लक्ष्यों में इस तरह अपनाया जा सकता है कि हम परिणाम की चिंता में उलझने के बजाय अपना पूरा प्रयास करें।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Focus on performing your duty with care rather than becoming attached to the results; meet success and failure with an even mind.

source_text: In this world, O Arjuna, a twofold path has been taught before by Me; the path of knowledge (jñāna-yoga) for men of discrimination(sāmkhyas) and the path of works (karma-yoga) for men of action (yogins).Not by abstention from actions does a man gain freedom, and not by mere renunciation does he attain perfection.No one can remain, even for a moment, without performing some action. Everyone is made to act helplessly by the gu as born of prak ti.He who controls his organs of action, but dwells in his mind on the objects of the senses; that man is deluded and is called a hypocrite.But he who controls the senses by the mind, O Arjuna, and, without attachment, engages the organs of action in karma-yoga, he excels.Perform thy allotted work, for action is superior to inaction; even the maintenance of thy body cannot be accomplished without action.This world is in bondage to karma, unless karma is performed for the sake of sacrifice. For the sake of that, O Arjuna, perform thyaction free from attachment.
source_summary: Krishna explains that avoiding action is not the way to achieve freedom or perfection. The passage emphasizes carrying out one's responsibilities instead of simply withdrawing from them.
english_explanation: Krishna explains that avoiding action is not the way to achieve freedom or perfection. The passage emphasizes carrying out one's responsibilities instead of simply withdrawing from them.
hindi_explanation: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि कर्म से पूरी तरह बचना मुक्ति या पूर्णता का मार्ग नहीं है। यह प्रसंग अपनी जिम्मेदारियों से पीछे हटने के बजाय उन्हें निभाने के महत्व को दर्शाता है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Freedom is not achieved merely by avoiding action; perform necessary responsibilities without attachment.

source_text: There is nothing in the three worlds, O Arjuna, to be done by Me,nor anything unobtained that needs to be obtained; yet I continue in action.For if I, unwearied, were not always in action, O Arjuna, men everywhere would follow my path (example).If I did not perform action, these worlds would be destroyed, and I should be the author of confusion and would destroy these people.As the ignorant act with attachment to their work, O Arjuna, so the wise man should act but without attachment, desiring to maintain the order of the world.Let no wise man unsettle the minds of the ignorant who are attached to action. Acting with discipline, he should make all action attractive.All actions are performed by the gunas of prakrti alone. But he who is deluded by egoism thinks, “I am the doer.”He who knows the true essence of the separation of the soul from both the gunas and action, O Arjuna, and that it is the gunas which act upon the gunas, he is not attached to action.Those who are deluded by the gu as of prakrti are attached to the action of the gunas. But the man who knows the whole should not unsettle the ignorant who know only a part.Surrendering all actions to Me, with thy consciousness fixed on the supreme Self, being free from desire and selfishness, fight freed from thy sorrow.
source_summary: Krishna explains that wise people should continue performing their responsibilities without selfish attachment. They should not act from ego or believe that they alone are the doers. Their actions should contribute to the welfare and stability of the world.
english_explanation: This passage teaches us to perform our responsibilities without excessive ego or selfish attachment. At work or in family life, we can focus on doing what is right instead of constantly seeking recognition or control.
hindi_explanation: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि बुद्धिमान व्यक्ति को अहंकार और स्वार्थपूर्ण आसक्ति के बिना अपने कर्तव्यों का पालन करना चाहिए। हमें केवल अपनी प्रशंसा या नियंत्रण की इच्छा से काम नहीं करना चाहिए, बल्कि अपने कार्यों से दूसरों और समाज के हित का भी ध्यान रखना चाहिए।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Act without selfish attachment or ego, and let your actions contribute to the welfare and order of the world.

source_text: Then by what is a man impelled to (commit) sin against his will, as if compelled by force, O krsna?The Blessed Lord said:This is desire, this is wrath, born of the gu a of passion, all devouring and very sinful. Know that this is the enemy here.As fire is covered by smoke, as a mirror by dust, and as an embryo is enveloped by the womb, so this knowledge is covered by that passion.Knowledge is enveloped, O Arjuna, by this constant enemy of the knower, by this insatiable flame of desire.The senses, the mind, the understanding are said to be its basis.With these it bewilders the embodied soul, covering its knowledge.Therefore, O Arjuna, having in the beginning controlled thy senses, slay this evil destroyer of spiritual and practical knowledge.
source_summary: Arjuna asks what drives a person to act wrongly even against their own wishes. Krishna identifies desire and anger as powerful forces that obscure knowledge. He explains how these forces influence the senses, mind and understanding, and advises controlling the senses.
english_explanation: This passage explores how uncontrolled desire and anger can influence our decisions. When strong emotions take over, we may act against our own values. Developing awareness and self-control can help us respond more thoughtfully.
hindi_explanation: अर्जुन पूछते हैं कि व्यक्ति अपनी इच्छा के विरुद्ध भी गलत कार्य करने के लिए क्यों प्रेरित होता है। कृष्ण इसका कारण अत्यधिक इच्छा और क्रोध को बताते हैं, जो हमारी समझ को ढक देते हैं। यह प्रसंग अपनी इंद्रियों और मन पर नियंत्रण रखने के महत्व को समझाता है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Desire and anger can obscure understanding; awareness and discipline of the senses help prevent impulsive action.

source_text: What is action? What is inaction? About this even the wise are confused. Therefore I will declare to thee what action is, knowing which thou shalt be freed from evil.One must understand the nature of action, and one must understand the nature of wrong action, and one must understand the nature of inaction: hard to understand is the way of action.He who sees inaction in action and action in inaction, he is wise among men; he does all actions harmoniously.He whose undertakings are all free from desire and will, whose actions are burned up in the fire of knowledge, him the wise call learned.Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, always content and independent, he does nothing even though he is engaged in action.Having no desires, with his mind and self controlled, abandoning all possessions, performing action with the body alone, he commits no sin.He who is content with what comes by chance, who has passed beyond the pairs of opposites, who is free from jealousy and is indifferent to success and failure, even when he is acting he is not bound.The action of a man who is rid of attachment, who is liberated, whose mind is firmly established in knowledge, who performs action as a sacrifice, is completely dissolved. .
source_summary: Krishna explains that the nature of action, wrong action and inaction is difficult to understand. A wise person understands action through knowledge and acts without attachment to results, desire or possessions. Such a person remains content and balanced in success and failure.
english_explanation: This passage encourages us to look beyond the surface of our actions and understand our intentions. We can remain active and responsible while reducing attachment, possessiveness and dependence on outcomes.
hindi_explanation: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि कर्म, विकर्म और अकर्म को सही रूप से समझना आसान नहीं है। ज्ञानी व्यक्ति अपने कार्यों को ज्ञान के साथ करता है और फल, इच्छा तथा संग्रह की आसक्ति से मुक्त रहने का प्रयास करता है। वह सफलता और असफलता में संतुलित रहता है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Understand the difference between action, wrong action and inaction; knowledge changes how action is performed and understood.

source_text: Even if thou art among sinners the worst sinner of all, thou shalt cross over all evil by the boat of knowledge alone.As the fire which is kindled makes its fuel into ashes, O Arjuna, so the fire of knowledge makes all actions into ashes.There is no purifier in this world equal to wisdom. He who is perfected in yoga finds it in the self in the course of time.He who has faith, who is intent on it (knowledge) and who has controlled his senses, obtains knowledge and having obtained it,goes quickly to the highest peace.But the ignorant man who is without faith and of a doubting nature perishes. For the doubting self, there is not this world, nor the next,nor happiness.Actions do not bind him who has renounced actions in yoga, who has cast away doubt by knowledge, who possesses himself, O Arjuna.Therefore having cut away, with the sword of knowledge, this doubt in thy heart that is born of ignorance, resort to yoga and arise,O Arjuna
source_summary: Krishna describes the power of knowledge and wisdom to overcome ignorance and doubt. He compares knowledge to fire that burns away the effects of actions and explains that faith, dedication and sense control help a person gain knowledge and peace.
english_explanation: This passage highlights the importance of learning, reflection and developing understanding. Doubt and confusion can hold us back, while sincere effort to gain knowledge can help us find clarity and inner peace.
hindi_explanation: कृष्ण ज्ञान की शक्ति को समझाते हैं, जो अज्ञान और संदेह को दूर कर सकता है। वे बताते हैं कि श्रद्धा, ज्ञान के प्रति समर्पण और इंद्रियों पर नियंत्रण व्यक्ति को समझ तथा आंतरिक शांति प्राप्त करने में सहायता करते हैं।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Knowledge and disciplined understanding can help a person move beyond doubt and find inner steadiness.

source_text: Arjuna said:Thou praisest renunciation of actions, O Krsna, and again (karma)yoga. Tell me definitely which one of these is the better.The Blessed Lord said:Renunciation (of works) and the unselfish performance of works(karma-yoga) both lead to the highest happiness. But of these two the unselfish performance of works is better than the renunciation of works.He who neither hates nor desires should be known as the eternal renouncer; free from the pairs of opposites, O Arjuna, he is easily released from bondage.Children, not the wise, speak of renunciation and yoga as separate;for he who is well established in one obtains the fruit of both.That place which is obtained by the sā khyas is also gained by the yogins. He who sees that sā khya and yoga are one, he truly sees.Renunciation, O Arjuna, is difficult to attain without yoga. The sage who is disciplined in yoga soon goes to Brahman.He who is disciplined in yoga and is pure in soul, who is ruler of his self, who has conquered his senses, whose self becomes the Self of all beings, he is not affected by acting.
source_summary: Arjuna asks whether renunciation or the path of action is better. Krishna explains that both can lead to the highest happiness, but selfless action is preferable. A disciplined person can perform actions without being bound by them.
english_explanation: This passage explains that spiritual growth does not necessarily require abandoning everyday responsibilities. A person can continue working and fulfilling duties while developing discipline, reducing selfish desires and maintaining inner balance.
hindi_explanation: अर्जुन पूछते हैं कि कर्मों का त्याग बेहतर है या कर्मयोग। कृष्ण बताते हैं कि दोनों मार्ग उच्च अवस्था तक ले जा सकते हैं, लेकिन निष्काम कर्म श्रेष्ठ है। व्यक्ति अपनी दैनिक जिम्मेदारियाँ निभाते हुए भी अनुशासन और आंतरिक संतुलन विकसित कर सकता है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Renunciation and selfless action need not be treated as opposites; responsible action can be performed without attachment.

source_text: The self-luminous Self (Ātman) imagines Itself through Itself by the power of its own illusion. It is itself the cognizer of objects.This is the definite conclusion of the Vedānta. As a rope which is not clearly perceived is, in the dark, imagined to be a snake or a line of water, so the Self is imagined in different ways. As definite knowledge of the rope destroys all illusions about it and the conviction arises that it is nothing but a rope, so is the nature of the Self determined.
source_summary: Gauḍapāda describes the Self as self-luminous. Through its own power of appearance, the Self may seem to be an individual experiencer. The rope-and-snake analogy illustrates how the Self can be misunderstood, just as a rope may be mistaken for a snake. Clear knowledge removes the mistaken perception.
english_explanation: In Advaita Vedanta, the Self (Ātman) is not merely the body, thoughts, or changing emotions. It is the underlying awareness through which experiences are known. Confusion about our identity can be compared to mistaking a rope for a snake in dim light. Understanding what is actually present removes the mistaken belief.
hindi_explanation: अद्वैत वेदांत के अनुसार आत्मा केवल शरीर, विचार या बदलती भावनाएँ नहीं है। यह वह मूल चेतना है जिसके माध्यम से सभी अनुभव जाने जाते हैं। हमारी वास्तविक पहचान को गलत समझना अँधेरे में रस्सी को साँप समझने जैसा है। सही ज्ञान से यह भ्रम दूर होता है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: The Self is often mistaken for changing appearances; like mistaking a rope for a snake, clear knowledge removes this misidentification.

source_text: Reality is Brahman which is without a second and is Existence, Consciousness and Bliss [saccidānanda]. Unreality is Nescience and all other material objects
source_summary: Sadānanda identifies Brahman as the non-dual Reality, described as Existence, Consciousness and Bliss (saccidānanda). The passage contrasts this Reality with ignorance and material objects.
english_explanation: Brahman is described in Advaita Vedanta as the ultimate, non-dual Reality. It is not one object among other objects. The expression Sat-Chit-Ananda points to existence, consciousness, and bliss as descriptions of this Reality.
hindi_explanation: अद्वैत वेदांत में ब्रह्म को परम और अद्वैत सत्य कहा गया है। यह अन्य वस्तुओं में से कोई एक वस्तु नहीं है। सत्-चित्-आनंद शब्द ब्रह्म के अस्तित्व, चेतना और आनंद स्वरूप को व्यक्त करते हैं।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Brahman is described as non-dual Reality, Existence, Consciousness and Bliss, beyond the changing world of material objects.

source_text: However, ignorance is described as something positive though intangible, which cannot be described either as being or nonbeing, which is made of three qualities and is antagonistic to Knowledge. Its existence is established from such experiences as, “Iam ignorant,” and from such śruti passages as, “The power belonging to God Himself, hidden in its own qualities” (Śve. Up. 1, 3).This ignorance is said to be one or many according to the mode of observing it either collectively or individually. As, for instance, trees considered as an aggregate are denoted as one, viz., the forest, or water is collectively named as the reservoir, so also ignorance, existing in jīvas, being diversely manifested,is collectively represented as one,—as in such scriptural passages as,“There is one unborn etc.” (Śve. Up. 4, 5).This aggregate (of ignorance) on account of its appearing associated with Perfection (Pure Intelligence of Brahman) has a preponderance of pure sattva.Consciousness associated with this is endowed with such qualities as omniscience, universal lordship, all-controlling power, etc., and is designated as the undifferentiated, the inner guide, the cause of the world and Īśvara on account of Its being the illuminator of the aggregate of ignorance. As in the śruti passage, “Who knows all (generally) who perceives all (particularly)” (Mu. Up. 1, 1, 9). This aggregate of ignorance associated with Īśvara is known as the causal body on account of its being the cause of all, and as the ānandamayakośa (the blissful sheath) on account of its being full of bliss and covering like a sheath; it is further known as the Cosmic sleep as into it everything is dissolved, and, for this reason, it is designated as the state of dissolution of the gross and subtle phenomena.As a forest, from the standpoint of the units that compose it,may be designated as a number of trees, and as a reservoir from the same point of view may be spoken of as quantities of water, so also ignorance when denoting separate units is spoken of as many; as in such śruti passages as, “Indra through Māyā appears as of many forms” ( gveda 6, 47, 18).Ignorance has been designated as individual and collective on account of its pervading the units and the aggregate. The individual ignorance, on account of its association with the inferior being, is characterized by impure sattva.
source_summary: Sadānanda describes ignorance as something that cannot simply be classified as either being or non-being. It is opposed to Knowledge and is discussed from both collective and individual standpoints. The text uses the analogy of a forest and its individual trees to explain these two standpoints.
english_explanation: Avidyā means ignorance or lack of true understanding. In Advaita Vedanta, it is associated with misunderstanding our true nature and perceiving reality through limitation and confusion. Sadānanda explains that ignorance can be considered collectively as well as individually.
hindi_explanation: अविद्या का अर्थ अज्ञान या सही समझ का अभाव है। अद्वैत वेदांत में इसे अपने वास्तविक स्वरूप को न समझ पाने और वास्तविकता को सीमित दृष्टि से देखने से जोड़ा जाता है। सदानंद अज्ञान को व्यक्तिगत और सामूहिक, दोनों दृष्टियों से समझाते हैं।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Ignorance or misapprehension veils understanding; discerning the Self from what is mistakenly attributed to it is central to knowledge.

source_text: As a rope which is not clearly perceived is, in the dark, imagined to be a snake or a line of water, so the Self is imagined in different ways. As definite knowledge of the rope destroys all illusions about it and the conviction arises that it is nothing but a rope, so is the nature of the Self determined.
source_summary: Gauḍapāda uses the rope-and-snake analogy to show how definite knowledge of the rope removes the mistaken perception of a snake. Similarly, knowledge of the Self removes mistaken understanding about our true nature.
core_teaching: Clear knowledge removes mistaken perception, just as recognising a rope removes the mistaken impression that it is a snake.
english_explanation: Vidya or Jnana means knowledge or understanding. In this context, it is not simply collecting information. It means seeing things clearly and recognising what is true. Just as knowing that an object is a rope removes the mistaken idea that it is a snake, self-knowledge removes misunderstanding about our true nature.
hindi_explanation: विद्या या ज्ञान का अर्थ सही समझ है। यहाँ इसका अर्थ केवल जानकारी इकट्ठा करना नहीं, बल्कि सत्य को स्पष्ट रूप से पहचानना है। जैसे किसी वस्तु को रस्सी जान लेने पर साँप का भ्रम मिट जाता है, वैसे ही आत्मज्ञान से अपने वास्तविक स्वरूप के बारे में गलत समझ दूर होती है।
practical_situations: Seeking clarity before making a decision
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta

source_text: When the empirical self (jīva) is awakened from the sleep of beginningless illusion (māyā), it realizes the unborn, sleepless,dreamless non-dual (Reality).If the phenomenal world were (really) existing then it ought no doubt to disappear. But this (whole universe of) duality is mere illusion: the absolute truth is that of non-duality.If anyone merely imagined the world of diversity (to exist), it would disappear (upon the termination of his fancy). This talk (of duality) is only for instruction. There is no duality (when Reality) is known.
source_summary: The introduction to Gauḍapāda's selections discusses the appearance of a world of duality and the doctrine of non-origination. In verses I.16-18, Gauḍapāda describes the world of diversity as imagined and explains that the appearance of duality disappears when Reality is known.
english_explanation: Māyā is associated with the appearance of multiplicity and the way reality seems to be divided into separate things. Gauḍapāda uses the language of illusion and imagination to explain the appearance of duality. This does not mean that everyday experiences should be ignored; it points to the difference between appearances and the non-dual Reality described by Advaita.
hindi_explanation: माया को अनेकता के आभास और वास्तविकता को अलग-अलग वस्तुओं के रूप में देखने से जोड़ा जाता है। गौड़पाद भ्रम और कल्पना के उदाहरणों से द्वैत के आभास को समझाते हैं। इसका अर्थ रोज़मर्रा के अनुभवों को अनदेखा करना नहीं, बल्कि दिखाई देने वाली अनेकता और अद्वैत सत्य के बीच अंतर समझना है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Gauḍapāda describes perceived multiplicity as appearance and presents non-duality as the truth realised when the appearance of duality is understood.

source_text: . The good is one thing, the gratifying is another;their goals are different, both bind a man.Good things await him who picks the good;By choosing the gratifying, one misses one’s goal.Both the good and the gratifying present themselves to a man;The wise assess them, note their difference;And choose the good over the gratifying;But the fool chooses the gratifying
source_summary: Yama explains the difference between what is genuinely beneficial and what is immediately pleasurable. A wise person recognises the difference and chooses what is beneficial, while an unwise person is drawn towards immediate gratification.
english_explanation: Not everything that feels good in the moment is necessarily good for us in the long run. This teaching encourages us to pause, consider the consequences and choose what supports our long-term well-being and growth.
hindi_explanation: यम बताते हैं कि जो चीज़ तुरंत सुख देती है, वह हमेशा हमारे लिए लाभदायक नहीं होती। समझदार व्यक्ति तत्काल सुख और वास्तविक हित के बीच अंतर पहचानकर सही विकल्प चुनता है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Distinguish what is genuinely beneficial from what is merely pleasant in the moment, and choose the good over immediate gratification.

source_text: What you call a treasure, I know to be transient;for by fleeting things one cannot attain the perennial.Therefore I have built the fire altar of Naciketas,and by things eternal I have gained the eternal.(Death)Satisfying desires is the foundation of the world;Uninterrupted rites bring ultimate security;Great and widespread praise is the foundation—these you have seen, wise Naciketas,and having seen, firmly rejected
source_summary: Naciketas recognises that wealth, possessions and worldly pleasures are temporary. He understands that temporary things cannot provide what is eternal and chooses the pursuit of deeper knowledge instead.
english_explanation: Material possessions and achievements can provide temporary satisfaction, but they cannot answer every deeper question about life. This passage encourages reflection on what gives life lasting meaning.
hindi_explanation: नचिकेता समझते हैं कि धन, संपत्ति और सांसारिक सुख अस्थायी हैं। वे पहचानते हैं कि अस्थायी वस्तुओं से शाश्वत सत्य की प्राप्ति नहीं हो सकती और इसलिए गहरे ज्ञान को प्राथमिकता देते हैं।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Temporary wealth and pleasures cannot provide what is eternal; examine whether external achievements answer deeper questions of meaning.

source_text: The primeval one who is hard to perceive,wrapped in mystery hidden in the cave,residing within the impenetrable depth—Regarding him as god, an insight gained by inner contemplation,both sorrow and joy the wise abandon.When a mortal has heard it, understood it;when he has drawn it out;and grasped this subtle point of doctrine,he rejoices, for he has found something in which he could rejoice.To him I consider my house to be open, Naciketas.
source_summary: The teaching describes the inner Self as subtle and hidden within the heart. Through inner contemplation and understanding, a wise person moves beyond sorrow and joy and discovers a deeper source of fulfilment.
english_explanation: Instead of depending entirely on external circumstances for happiness, this teaching encourages us to develop inner awareness and reflection. Understanding our deeper nature can help us relate differently to changing experiences.
hindi_explanation: यह शिक्षा बताती है कि आत्मा हमारे भीतर विद्यमान है और उसे बाहरी वस्तुओं से नहीं, बल्कि आत्मचिंतन से समझा जा सकता है। आंतरिक समझ विकसित होने पर व्यक्ति सुख और दुख से परे गहरी शांति का अनुभव कर सकता है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Inner contemplation and understanding of the subtle Self are associated with moving beyond the hold of sorrow and joy.

source_text: 18. The wise one—he is not born, he does not die;he has not come from anywhere;He is the unborn and eternal, primeval and everlasting.And he is not killed, when the body is killed.(The dialogue between Naciketas and Death appears to end here.)If the killer thinks that he kills;If the killed thinks that he is killed;Both of them fail to understand.He neither kills, nor is he killed.Finer than the finest, larger than the largest,is the self (Ātman) that lies here hidden in the heart of a living being.Without desires and free from sorrow,a man perceives by the creator's grace the grandeur of the self.Sitting down, he roams afar.Lying down, he goes everywhere.The god ceaselessly exulting— Who, besides me, is able to know?When he perceives this immense, all-pervading self,as bodiless within bodies,as stable within unstable beings—A wise man ceases to grieve.This self cannot be grasped,by teachings or by intelligence,or even by great learning.Only the man he chooses can grasp him,Whose body this self chooses as his own
source_summary: The passage describes the Self as unborn, eternal and not destroyed when the body dies. It is subtle, present within living beings and not understood merely through intellectual learning. Realising the Self is associated with freedom from grief.
english_explanation: The teaching distinguishes the eternal Self from the changing physical body. It invites us to look beyond physical identity and recognise the deeper nature of the Self.
hindi_explanation: यह प्रसंग आत्मा को अजन्मा, शाश्वत और शरीर के नष्ट होने पर भी अविनाशी बताता है। यह हमें केवल शरीर को अपनी पहचान मानने के बजाय आत्मा के गहरे स्वरूप को समझने के लिए प्रेरित करता है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: The Self is described as unborn and eternal; recognising it as distinct from the body is associated with freedom from grief.

source_text: Sages look equally on a brahmin endowed with knowledge and breeding, or on a cow, an elephant, and even a dog and an outcaste.Even here on earth, creation is conquered by those whose minds are established in equality. Brahman is spotless and is the same to all.Therefore they are established in Brahman.One should not rejoice when obtaining the pleasant, nor be agitated when obtaining the unpleasant. Unbewildered, with firm intelligence, the knower of Brahman is established in Brahman.The self who is unattached to external contacts finds happiness in the Self. Being joined by yoga to Brahman, he attains imperishable happiness.The enjoyments which are born of contacts with objects are only sources of sorrow. These have a beginning and end, O Arjuna; the wise man does not rejoice in them.He who is able to endure here on earth, even before he is liberated from the body, the force that springs from desire and anger, he is disciplined, he is the happy man.He who is happy within, whose joy is within and whose light is within; that yogin becomes Brahman and attains to the bliss of Brahman.The seers whose sins are destroyed, whose dualities (doubts) are dispelled, whose selves are disciplined and who rejoice in the welfare of all beings, attain to the bliss of Brahman.To these holy men who have destroyed desire and anger, who have controlled their minds, who know the Self, the bliss of Brahman is near.
source_summary: Krishna describes the wise person as one who sees with equality, recognising Brahman as the same in all. Such a person is not carried away by pleasant experiences or disturbed by unpleasant ones and finds happiness within the Self.
english_explanation: This passage encourages us to look beyond external differences and treat others with fairness and understanding. It also teaches that lasting happiness should not depend entirely on pleasant circumstances.
hindi_explanation: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि ज्ञानी व्यक्ति सभी में एक ही ब्रह्म को देखता है और बाहरी भेदभाव से ऊपर उठता है। वह सुखद परिस्थितियों में अत्यधिक प्रसन्न और कठिन परिस्थितियों में विचलित नहीं होता तथा आंतरिक आनंद को पहचानता है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: See the same Brahman in all and remain steady through pleasant and unpleasant experiences; lasting happiness is found within.

source_text: Through knowledge of reality he brings samsāra to a halt.Right-knowledge destroys the path of renunciation as surely as it destroys the path of action.Through merely becoming aware of the Self once one destroys the whole of sa sāra, through negation of ignorance once and for all. There is no more wrong knowledge afterwards.Time and space etc. are the effects of delusion, and do not inhere in the Self. Once the Self is known, there is no more knowledge to gain and no ignorance left unconsumed.
source_summary: Maṇḍana Miśra explains that knowledge of Reality brings saṃsāra to an end. Awareness of the Self removes ignorance and mistaken understanding, while time and space are described as effects of delusion rather than attributes of the Self.
english_explanation: In Advaita Vedanta, freedom is associated with recognising the true nature of the Self. This passage explains that deeper understanding removes ignorance rather than merely adding more information.
hindi_explanation: मण्डन मिश्र बताते हैं कि वास्तविकता और आत्मा का सही ज्ञान अज्ञान तथा भ्रम को समाप्त करता है। अद्वैत वेदांत में मुक्ति का संबंध अपने वास्तविक स्वरूप को पहचानने से है।
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
core_teaching: Knowledge of the Self removes ignorance and mistaken understanding; in this passage, such knowledge is linked with the end of saṃsāra.

source_text: However, ignorance is described as something positive though intangible, which cannot be described either as being or non being, which is made of three qualities and is antagonistic to Knowledge. Its existence is established from such experiences as, “I am ignorant,” and from such śruti passages as, “The power belonging to God Himself, hidden in its own qualities”.
source_summary: Sadānanda describes ignorance as something positive though intangible, which cannot be described as either being or non-being. He explains that ignorance is opposed to Knowledge and is recognised through experiences such as 'I am ignorant.'
core_teaching: Ignorance is described as opposed to Knowledge, and its presence is recognised through experiences of not knowing.
english_explanation: Sadānanda explains ignorance as something that cannot be simply described as either being or non-being. It is opposed to Knowledge and is recognised through experiences such as thinking, 'I am ignorant.' This passage introduces the Advaita Vedānta understanding of ignorance.
hindi_explanation: सदानन्द अज्ञान को ऐसी अवस्था के रूप में समझाते हैं जिसे सरलता से अस्तित्ववान या अनस्तित्ववान नहीं कहा जा सकता। यह ज्ञान के विपरीत है और इसका अनुभव 'मैं अज्ञानी हूँ' जैसी भावना से पहचाना जा सकता है। यह अज्ञान के अद्वैत वेदान्त संबंधी विचार को समझाता है।
practical_situations: Recognising the limits of one's understanding
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta

topic: Fear of loss, change and impermanence
source_text: Thou grievest for those thou shouldst not grieve for, and yet thouspeakest words that sound like wisdom. Wise men do not mourn for the dead or for the living.Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor thou, nor these rulers of men; nor will there ever be a time hereafter when we shall all cease to be.As the soul in the body passes through childhood, youth and old age, so (after departure from this body) it passes on to another body.The sage is not bewildered by this.Contacts with the objects of the senses, O Arjuna, give rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go, they are impermanent; endure them, O Arjuna.The man who is not troubled by these contacts, O Arjuna, who treats alike pleasure and pain, who is wise; he is fit for immortality.Of non-being there is no coming to be; of being there is no ceasing to be. The truth about both is seen by the seers of truth.Know that by which all this is pervaded is indestructible, and that no one can cause the destruction of this immutable being.It is said that (only) these bodies of the eternal embodied soul,which is indestructible and incomprehensible, are perishable.Therefore fight, O Arjuna!He who thinks that this soul is a slayer, and he who thinks that this soul is slain; both of them are ignorant. This soul neither slays nor is slain.It is never born, nor does it die, nor having once been, will it again cease to be. It is unborn, eternal, and everlasting. This primeval one is not slain when the body is slain.He who knows that it is indestructible and eternal, unborn and unchanging, how can that man slay, O Arjuna, or cause another to slay?Just as a man casts off worn-out clothes and takes on others that are new, so the embodied soul casts off worn-out bodies and takes on others that are new.Weapons do not cut it, nor does fire burn it; waters do not make it wet, nor does wind make it dry.It is uncleavable; it cannot be burnt, it can neither be wetted nor dried. It is eternal, omnipresent, unchanging and immovable. It is everlasting.It is called unmanifest, unthinkable and immutable; therefore,knowing it as such, thou shouldst not grieve.
source_summary: Krishna explains the distinction between the eternal Self and the perishable body, and discusses the temporary nature of pleasure and pain.
core_teaching: The Self is described as eternal, while bodily experiences and worldly conditions are subject to change.
english_explanation: This teaching can provide a philosophical perspective when reflecting on loss, change and uncertainty. It distinguishes the enduring Self from changing experiences, without suggesting that human grief or emotional pain should simply be ignored.
hindi_explanation: श्रीकृष्ण शाश्वत आत्मा और नश्वर शरीर के बीच अंतर समझाते हैं। वे सुख और दुख को भी परिवर्तनशील अनुभव बताते हैं। यह शिक्षा जीवन में बदलाव और हानि पर दार्शनिक दृष्टि से विचार करने में सहायता कर सकती है।
practical_situations: Fear of losing a loved one
source_book: The Essential Vedanta: A New Source Book of Advaita Vedanta
